policy.sourceAuthority: Fresh authored synthetic records. Host record sequence and explicit backward supersession determine active eligibility, never model inference.
policy.candidateConstruction: Every annotated whole title/narrator span pairs with every requested item in source order then item order. Title equality and active-source eligibility are unchanged from V5. No gold-filtered candidates or inferred extra spans.
policy.exactGrammar: Unchanged V5 canonicalSupportStatement and exactSupportsCandidate; four canonical controls retain that exact syntax so the frozen parser has a recognized surface.
policy.novelty: New identities throughout. The remaining sixteen cases use new multi-line catalogs, production ledgers, recorded credits, roster notation, role separation, qualification and attribution contexts. This is a designed mechanism cohort, not representative memory quality.
policy.semanticTask: Unchanged V5 supported/contradicted/uncertain prompt and one decision per eligible candidate. Same decisions feed the unguarded and subtractively guarded programs.
policy.goldIsolation: V7_GOLD is separate from buildFixtures output. Family rationale and supporting IDs belong only to gold and must not enter candidate construction or provider requests.
policy.goldComparison: Recommended items require exact title/narrator. Unknown, omitted-incomplete and conflict compare status only; candidate support and retained partial fields are assessed separately. Conflict may be the correct outcome for distinct current admitted narrator values.
policy.limits: Exactly twenty complete cases. No clipping, truncation, candidate sampling or cases dropped to fit a bound. Every field is <=256 UTF-8 bytes and each complete source program input <=256 KiB.

gold.mechanism: Positive exact-grammar utility and subject ownership across distinct directional suffixes; cross-item narration proposals are unsupported.
Two current records agree on one narrator; preserve both source witnesses without inventing a conflict or losing usefulness.
Locked identifiers are byte-distinct composed/decomposed Unicode; only exact subject ownership supports each candidate. No normalization is authorized.
Identical numbers with different title units remain different identities; no unit conversion or approximate matching is allowed.
Catalog labels and final-credit status explicitly identify title and narrator without the canonical sentence grammar.
Source presents factual opening/closing credits of the released recording; read-aloud credit for the whole audiobook establishes narration.
The table header and single row bind the narrator column to the audiobook column without relying on nearby names.
A named source speaker explicitly states they are the credited complete-book narrator; the same statement binds speaker and recording.
An explicit narrator designation supports the speaking performer; the fact is not inferred merely from performance relevance.
Completed, final narrator assignments support two ownership edges. One requested item deliberately has no annotated title candidate; locked request identity is not field evidence.
A sentence explicitly distinguishes booklet editing from narration; the annotated narrator value follows the narration credit only.
Two labeled business-card style source records establish their stated fields for the same released audiobook.
An exclusion entry refutes narrator support. Both title-only items remain incomplete, with requested and optional modes requiring distinct outcomes.
The person fills a sound-engineer slot while the narrator slot is explicitly unrecorded; role membership cannot be transferred.
Both current sources individually establish different narrator credits and neither supersedes the other. The single-valued program must preserve the conflict rather than pick a source.
Explicit backward host links form a three-revision chain. Only the final source remains eligible; the older narrator candidates stay in the full inventory but are inactive.
An unrealized conditional role is not a current narration attribution. No current narrator is supplied.
The complete statement explicitly rejects the quoted draft attribution; recognizing an embedded name cannot override the rejection.
One person is narrator of one book and explicitly producer, not narrator, of the other. Cross-pair construction must retain and reject the wrong-owner proposal.
Licensing and administrative ownership supply neither title evidence in the restricted inventory nor narration. All-unknown control cannot earn useful recommendation credit.

interpretation: All source records are newly authored synthetic fixtures, with supplied spans, locked identities and host eligibility. This replays captured admissions and deterministic program behavior; it does not rerun Jev or the writer, prove semantic entailment, or establish broad generalization. The observed guarded gain is concentrated in the case that deliberately treats canonically equivalent Unicode title strings as distinct locked identities; this is a host identity policy, not a normal bibliographic assumption. Missing annotated title support also remains missing despite a matching request display title. All twenty original cases and gold remain unchanged. Gold is retained separately and never used for admission or veto.
